cable_to_cable.note: 3D distance is never below the plan distance, so the plan bound holds in every state

envelope.basis: core outline XY from the mated DIN plane to the handle tops plus the 40 mm withdrawal

core_40mm.procedure: K-PWR first, then 40 mm along +z; J-SIG/J-PWR are not touched
core_40mm.registration: core carrier to middle/jack carrier registration UNCONFIRMED (panel_to_carrier_registration_mm null in Stage32); not in the stack

J-PWR.excludes: the boards carrying the cable ends (their clearance is the housing height, not a lateral gap)
J-PWR.shared_gap: the cable-to-cable plan gap is shared: if both arches lean toward each other the sum of both deviations must stay within it

J-SIG.excludes: the boards carrying the cable ends (their clearance is the housing height, not a lateral gap)
J-SIG.nearest: the other cable (plan bound, both arches in their planes)
J-SIG.shared_gap: the cable-to-cable plan gap is shared: if both arches lean toward each other the sum of both deviations must stay within it

friction.note: the retention bounds do not use stiffness; this only shows the slack can follow a withdrawal without buckling a free span. The drag bound (friction x weight) leaves out contact forces from bending stiffness and tension at the bends. Abrasion over repeated withdrawals is not calculated (M34-04).
